# 1 Kings Chapter 17 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-Elijah the-Tishbite, from-the-settlers-of Gilead, said to-Ahab, "As-YHWH lives, the-God-of Israel, before-whom I-stand, there-shall-not be these-years dew or-rain, except by the-word-of my-mouth."

**2** And-the-word-of YHWH came to-him, saying,

**3** "Go from-here and-turn eastward and-hide-yourself by-the-brook Cherith, that is before the-Jordan.

**4** And-it-shall-be — from-the-brook you-shall-drink, and-ʾet-the-ravens I-have-commanded to-provide-for-you there."

**5** And-he-went and-did according-to-the-word-of YHWH. And-he-went and-dwelt by-the-brook Cherith, that is before the-Jordan.

**6** And-the-ravens were-bringing to-him bread and-meat in-the-morning, and-bread and-meat in-the-evening, and-from the-brook he-drank.

**7** And-it-was at-the-end-of days, and-the-brook dried-up, for there-had-been no rain in-the-land.

**8** And-the-word-of YHWH came to-him, saying,

**9** "Arise, go to-Zarephath, that belongs-to-Sidon, and-dwell there. Behold, I-have-commanded there a-widow woman to-provide-for-you."

**10** And-he-arose and-went to-Zarephath and-came to the-entrance-of the-city, and-behold — a-widow woman there gathering sticks. And-he-called to-her and-said, "Bring to-me, please, a-little water in-a-vessel, and-I-will-drink."

**11** And-she-went to-bring-it, and-he-called to-her and-said, "Bring to-me, please, a-morsel-of bread in-your-hand."

**12** And-she-said, "As-YHWH your-God lives, I-have-no cake — only a-handful-of flour in-the-jar and-a-little oil in-the-jug. And-behold, I am-gathering two sticks, and-I-will-go and-make-it for-me and-for-my-son, and-we-will-eat-it and-die."

**13** And-Elijah said to-her, "Do-not fear. Go, do according-to-your-word. But first make for-me from-there a-small cake, and-bring-it-out to-me. And-for-you and-for-your-son you-shall-make afterward.

**14** For thus says YHWH, the-God-of Israel: 'The-jar-of flour shall-not be-finished and-the-jug-of oil shall-not lack, until the-day YHWH gives rain upon the-face-of the-earth.'"

**15** And-she-went and-did according-to-the-word-of Elijah. And-she-ate — she and-he and-her-household — for-days.

**16** The-jar-of flour was-not finished and-the-jug-of oil did-not lack, according-to-the-word-of YHWH that he-spoke by-the-hand-of Elijah.

**17** And-it-was after these things, and-the-son-of the-woman, the-mistress-of the-house, became-sick. And-his-sickness was very severe, until there-was-no breath left in-him.

**18** And-she-said to-Elijah, "What is-to-me and-to-you, man-of God? You-came to-me to-bring-to-remembrance ʾet-my-iniquity and-to-cause-my-son-to-die!"

**19** And-he-said to-her, "Give to-me ʾet-your-son." And-he-took-him from-her-bosom and-carried-him-up to the-upper-room where he was-dwelling, and-laid-him on his-bed.

**20** And-he-called to YHWH and-said, "YHWH my-God, have-you also brought-evil upon the-widow with-whom I am-sojourning, to-cause-her-son-to-die?"

**21** And-he-stretched-himself upon the-child three times, and-called to YHWH, and-said, "YHWH my-God, please let-return the-life-of this child upon his-inward-parts."

**22** And-YHWH heard the-voice-of Elijah, and-the-life-of the-child returned upon his-inward-parts, and-he-lived.

**23** And-Elijah took ʾet-the-child and-brought-him-down from the-upper-room to-the-house, and-gave-him to-his-mother. And-Elijah said, "See — your-son lives."

**24** And-the-woman said to-Elijah, "Now this I-know, that a-man-of God you are, and-the-word-of YHWH in-your-mouth is truth."

---
## EMET Textual Notes

1. **17:1 — "before-whom I-stand"**: Elijah's self-identification — he stands in YHWH's presence as a servant before a king. This phrase defines the prophetic office as intimate access to the divine court.

2. **17:6 — ravens**: The Hebrew ʿorvim (ravens) are unclean birds (Lev 11:15), yet God commands them to feed his prophet. Provision comes through ritually impure channels — a theological provocation.

3. **17:9 — Zarephath/Sidon**: YHWH sends Elijah to Jezebel's homeland — Sidonian territory. God provides for his prophet through a foreign widow in the very region from which Israel's corruption came.

4. **17:18 — "What is-to-me and-to-you?"**: A formula of confrontation — "What do we have in common?" or "Why are you involving yourself with me?" The widow interprets Elijah's presence as divine judgment on her past sins.

5. **17:21 — "stretched-himself upon"**: The first resurrection narrative in the Hebrew Bible. Elijah's bodily contact with the dead child transfers life — an intimate, physical act of prophetic intercession.

— EMET
